monster noun

also monstrosity, portent, prodigy, a monstrous thing

classical

Cic. Div. 1.93 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 2.1 (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 3.658 (Lewis & Short)

mōnstrum, mōnstrī n.

noun, second declension

an omen of evil, a portent; a monster, a monstrous thing

Examples

  • mōnstrum horrendum, īnfōrme, ingēns, cui lūmen adēmptum

    a monster, horrible, shapeless, huge, robbed of its eyeVerg. A. 3.658

See also sign.
